docs.title: Cobblemon PokeGyms
docs.text:
Not released yet

PokeGyms has no public download yet. These pages describe the current development build, 0.0.32. What it does today is find the gyms, give each City gym an RCT leader you can fight, let you challenge the leader of a player-held gym (a loser pays its penalty into the gym's vault, a winner gets a signed medal, a Badge It badge if the gym has one, and a challenger waits before a rematch), scale every RCT trainer's team, leaders included, to your level (stage and moves too), run their Gym Manager and tell other mods which battles are gym battles. Gym battle rules, taking a gym over and disciples are not in the mod yet, and nothing here describes them.

docs.title: Cobblemon PokeGyms
docs.text:
Gyms for Cobblemon multiplayer servers. PokeGyms finds the gym building of every Kanto city that Cobblemon Cities & Structures generates, records it for the world, and stands a Gym Manager inside its door: the one place where everything about that gym happens.

MC 1.21.1 Fabric NeoForge Not released yet Cobblemon 1.8+ Needs CobbleDollars + Radical Cobblemon Trainers + Cities & Structures

Get started The Gym Manager

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text:
• 🏙️ Every Cities & Structures gym, found: Pewter, Cerulean, Vermilion, Celadon, Fuchsia, Saffron, Cinnabar and Viridian, also in worlds generated before PokeGyms was installed.
  • 📖 A Gym Manager in every gym: a lectern just inside the door that opens the gym's own screen, titled by its city, such as "Pewter City Gym".
  • 🏛️ A Radical Cobblemon Trainers leader in every City gym: every gym starts as a City gym, led by one of RCT's own gym leaders.
  • 🥊 Fight the City leader: a stake of CobbleDollars, and it stays out of RCT's progression.
  • 🔓 Beat the leader, unlock the gym: only a player who beats a City leader may buy that gym's licence.
  • 🎫 Licences: the rules for owning a gym are in place, one licence per player on the whole server.
  • 💰 The gym vault: a player leader sets a penalty, a challenger who loses pays it into the gym's vault, and the holder withdraws it.
  • 🏅 Signed medals: beat a player leader and you get a Gym Medal that names the gym, the leader and the date, or a signed Badge It badge when the leader registered one.
  • 📈 Level scaling: a leader's team, and every RCT trainer's, fights at the level of your best Pokémon, up or down, evolution stage included, so a battle is fair at any stage.
  • ⚔️ Gym battles, recognised: a battle against a trainer inside a gym counts as a gym battle, so other mods can reward it, such as Mid-Battle EXP's extra EXP in gyms.
  • ⚙️ Tuned in game with /pokegyms config, no restart needed.

docs.title: Get it
docs.text:
Version 0.0.32 Minecraft 1.21.1 Side Server and every player's game Cobblemon 1.8+ — 1.7.x is not supported Also needs CobbleDollars, Radical Cobblemon Trainers, Cobblemon Cities & Structures — Radical Cobblemon Trainers with its RCT API. Without Cities & Structures PokeGyms starts but finds no gyms Fabric Fabric Language Kotlin, Architectury API NeoForge Kotlin for Forge, Architectury API Optional Badge It: the leader registers one of its badges as the gym's medal

No public download yet. New here? Start with Getting Started.

docs.title: Commands & Configuration
docs.text: Every command is under /pokegyms, for operators only (permission level 2).

docs.title: /pokegyms gyms
docs.text:
Lists every gym the server has found in your current dimension, one line each: its coordinates, its status (canonical, vacant, or held by a player), the city structure it stands in, and how many of its five marks PokeGyms read (5/5 markers is a healthy gym).

Click the coordinates to get a /tp to that gym's Gym Manager in your chat box.

docs.title: /pokegyms battles
docs.text: Lists the gym battles running now, one line each: the battle's id, who the challenger faces (leader, disciple or canonical_leader), and the gym's coordinates and dimension, as /pokegyms gyms lists them. With none running, it says No gym battles running.

docs.title: /pokegyms config
docs.text:
Shows and changes every setting on a live server. A change takes effect at once, without a restart, and is written to the config file so it survives one.

Command What it does /pokegyms config Lists every feature with its settings. /pokegyms config licences Lists one feature. A value that is not the default shows the default beside it. /pokegyms config licences enabled <true\|false> Switches the whole feature on or off. /pokegyms config licences <setting> <value> Sets a number, within the setting's range. /pokegyms config canonical penalty <value> The same for the City-leader battle; canonical takes enabled and reset like licences. /pokegyms config leader enabled <true\|false> Opens or closes team registration; leader has no numbers, and takes reset too. /pokegyms config vault <setting> <value> Sets penalty_min or penalty_max of the gym vault; vault takes enabled and reset too. /pokegyms config rematch <setting> <value> Sets cooldown_minutes of the rematch cooldown; rematch takes enabled and reset too. /pokegyms config scaling enabled <true\|false> Switches level scaling, of gym leaders and RCT trainers, on or off; scaling has no numbers, and takes reset too. /pokegyms config evolution enabled <true\|false> Switches the evolution stage of scaled teams on or off; needs scaling on, evolution has no numbers, and takes reset too. /pokegyms config medals enabled <true\|false> Switches the medal for beating a player leader on or off; medals has no numbers, and takes reset too. /pokegyms config licences reset Puts the feature back to its defaults, switched on.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
The settings live in config/cobblemon_pokegyms.json on the server:

{
  "licences": {
    "enabled": true,
    "price": 25000,
    "expiry_days": 30
  },
  "canonical": {
    "enabled": true,
    "penalty": 1000
  },
  "leader": {
    "enabled": true
  },
  "vault": {
    "enabled": true,
    "penalty_min": 100,
    "penalty_max": 10000
  },
  "rematch": {
    "enabled": true,
    "cooldown_minutes": 60
  },
  "scaling": {
    "enabled": true
  },
  "evolution": {
    "enabled": true
  },
  "medals": {
    "enabled": true
  }
}
Setting Default Range What it does licences.enabled true Off: no vacant gym sells its licence. Licences already held stay, and still expire or can be renounced. licences.price 25000 0 or more What a gym's licence costs, in CobbleDollars. licences.expiry_days 30 0 to 36,500 Days a holder can stay offline before their licence ends. 0 keeps a licence for good. canonical.enabled true Off: City gym leaders take no challenges. Battles already running finish, and a loss still costs the penalty. canonical.penalty 1000 0 or more What losing to a City leader costs, in CobbleDollars, and the least a challenger must carry to start. It is destroyed, never paid to anyone. leader.enabled true Off: no holder can register or replace their gym's team. Teams already registered stay, with their leader. vault.enabled true Off: no player leader charges a penalty and no challenger needs one. Vaults keep their money, can still be withdrawn, and are still paid out when a licence ends. vault.penalty_min 100 0 or more The least a holder may set as their gym's penalty, in CobbleDollars. A new holder starts on it. vault.penalty_max 10000 0 or more The most a holder may set as their gym's penalty. A range given the wrong way round counts from its smaller end. rematch.enabled true Off: a challenger may challenge a player leader again at once. Finished challenges are still recorded, so switching it back on counts them. rematch.cooldown_minutes 60 0 to 525,600 Minutes a challenger waits after a finished challenge, won or lost, before challenging that gym's leader again. 0 means no wait. scaling.enabled true Off: gym leaders' and RCT trainers' teams battle at the levels they were registered at, not at the challenger's. Battles already running keep theirs. evolution.enabled true Off: a scaled team keeps its registered species instead of taking the evolution stage of its new level. Needs scaling on. medals.enabled true Off: beating a player leader gives no medal. Medals already given stay.

A setting missing from the file takes its default, and one out of range is pulled into it; the file is then written back whole, so you always find every setting in it. A file that is not valid JSON is left as it is, and the server runs on the defaults and says so in its log.

See Licences for what a licence does.

docs.title: Community Credits
docs.text:
PokeGyms is built on the work of others:

  • Cobblemon, whose summary screen the Gym Manager is built on.
  • Cobblemon Cities & Structures, whose Kanto cities, gym buildings and leaders PokeGyms runs.
  • CobbleDollars, the currency gym licences are paid in.
  • Radical Cobblemon Trainers, whose trainers and API PokeGyms builds on.

Found a bug or have an idea? Post it in the Discord.

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text: PokeGyms targets Minecraft 1.21.1 on Fabric and NeoForge, with Cobblemon 1.8. It is made for multiplayer servers, and it goes on the server and on every player's game.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
Dependency Notes Minecraft 1.21.1 Fabric Loader 0.18.0+ or NeoForge the jar for your loader Fabric Language Kotlin or Kotlin for Forge the one for your loader Architectury API both loaders Cobblemon 1.8.0+ 1.7.x is not supported CobbleDollars 2.0.0+ the currency licences are paid in Radical Cobblemon Trainers 0.19.2-beta+ with its RCT API 0.16.2-beta+ Cobblemon Cities & Structures the cities whose gyms PokeGyms runs

Optional: Badge It, so a gym's medal can be one of its badges (Medals).

PokeGyms starts without Cities & Structures, but then it finds no gyms and does nothing. With an older version of any of the others, the game refuses to start and names the mod and the version it needs.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Install Cobblemon, CobbleDollars, Radical Cobblemon Trainers with RCT API, Cobblemon Cities & Structures and the libraries for your loader.
  2. Drop the PokeGyms jar for your loader into mods/, on the server and on every player's game. Never put both loaders' jars in.
  3. Start the server. Existing worlds work: a city generated before PokeGyms was installed has its gym found the first time it loads.
  4. Walk into the gym of a Cities & Structures Kanto city. The Gym Manager lectern stands just inside the door; right-click it.

An operator can list every gym the server has found in the current dimension with /pokegyms gyms (Commands).

docs.title: Which gyms
docs.text:
PokeGyms runs the gym buildings of Cobblemon Cities & Structures. Eight of its Kanto cities can have one:

Pewter · Cerulean · Vermilion · Celadon · Fuchsia · Saffron · Cinnabar · Viridian

Lavender and Pallet have no gym, and a city does not always build its gym, so not every city you find has one. That is Cities & Structures' choice; PokeGyms records the gyms that are there.

A gym is found the first time its city loads, new or generated long before PokeGyms was installed, and it is remembered for that world from then on, across restarts. Each dimension keeps its own list.

docs.title: City gyms and their leaders
docs.text:
Every gym starts as a City gym, led by one of Radical Cobblemon Trainers' own gym leaders (the leader_* trainers, 24 different names in RCT 0.19.2).

  • One leader per City, kept for good. PokeGyms picks the leader the first time the gym is found and remembers it. No leader's name repeats across the world's gyms until every one has been used.
  • The leader stands still and cannot be hurt, at the gym's leader spot. The Gym Manager names them.
  • Cities & Structures' own leader is removed. PokeGyms puts RCT's leader in their place, so the gym never has two. Worlds made before this version change over by themselves the next time each gym loads.
  • A gym that is no longer a City gym loses its RCT leader.

docs.title: Fighting a City leader
docs.text:
Right-click the leader to challenge them. PokeGyms starts the battle with the leader's RCT team, but it does not count in RCT's progression: winning does not raise your level cap or add the leader to your defeat list, and RCT gives no loot or dialogue for it.

  • You need CobbleDollars to start. You must carry at least the penalty, canonical.penalty (1,000 by default). If you are short, you are told how much you need.
  • Losing costs the penalty. Losing, forfeiting or running away takes exactly that sum from you. The money goes to no one. Winning costs nothing, and unlocks the gym's licence for you.
  • One challenger at a time per leader. A second challenger is told the leader is busy.
  • Operators can close the fight or change the penalty with /pokegyms config canonical. Closed, leaders take no challenges; battles already running finish, and a loss still costs the penalty.

docs.title: Unlocking a City gym
docs.text:
A City gym's licence is not for sale to everyone: only a player who beats its leader in the fight above may buy it (see Licences).

  • A win unlocks it for the winner only. You are told in chat, the Info tab says you may buy the licence, and the Licence tab appears. Everyone else who opens the Gym Manager is told to beat the leader first, and the server refuses their purchase.
  • Nothing else counts. Losing, running away, a battle that is stopped, or beating the leader outside PokeGyms' own fight unlocks nothing.
  • The leader steps aside while the gym is held. When the winner buys the licence, the RCT leader leaves the gym and takes no challenge.
  • When the licence ends, the leader returns. Renouncing or expiring puts the leader back and locks the gym again for everyone, the former holder included: they must beat the leader anew.
  • Your win is remembered even if licences are switched off, so it still counts when they are switched back on.

docs.title: Registering your team
docs.text:
A gym's holder (the player who holds its licence, in a town gym or in a City gym won from its leader) can register their party as the gym's team. The gym then has a leader of its own.

  • Open the Team tab of the Gym Manager, pick singles or doubles, and press Register. Singles takes 1 Pokémon from your party, doubles takes 2. Only the holder sees the tab, and the server checks it again when you press the button.
  • The gym keeps a frozen copy. The Pokémon are copied, healed, and the copy does not follow yours: you keep your own Pokémon and can train, trade or lose them. Registering again replaces the copy.
  • Everyone sees the team. The gym team panel on the Gym Manager's side lists the registered Pokémon by name and level.
  • A leader NPC stands for it. Gym Leader stands at the gym's leader spot, wearing the holder's skin (default or slim, read from their Minecraft profile) and carrying the copy as its party. It cannot be hurt, moved or pushed, and does not despawn. If it is killed, it comes back the next time its chunk loads.
  • It leaves when the licence ends. Renouncing or expiring removes the team and the NPC. In a City gym, the RCT leader returns at the same time (see Unlocking a City gym). An NPC whose chunk was unloaded when the licence ended is removed the next time that chunk loads.
  • Operators can close registration with /pokegyms config leader. Off, nobody can register or replace a team; teams already registered stay, with their leader.

    • Worlds saved before this version load every gym with no team. A saved team that cannot be read is dropped and the gym is kept.

docs.title: Challenging a gym
docs.text:
Right-click the Gym Leader NPC of a player-held gym to fight the team its holder registered.

  • The holder picks the format. It is singles or doubles, whatever the holder registered.
  • Who cannot challenge. The holder cannot challenge their own gym. A gym with no holder or no registered team takes no challenge, and neither does a leader who is already battling someone else (you are told it is busy).
  • You need the penalty in hand. The holder sets a penalty for their gym, and you must carry at least that many CobbleDollars to challenge. A loss moves exactly the penalty into the gym's vault; a win or a stopped battle costs nothing. If you are short, you are told how much it costs and what you have.
  • The result counts once. Winning or losing tells you in chat. Forfeiting or running away counts as a loss. A battle the server stops counts as nothing.
  • The leader always fields a fresh copy of the team. Used PP or berries from an earlier battle do not carry over, and the gym's registered team is never changed.
  • Nobody's Pokémon are hurt. The battle uses a copy of your party, so your Pokémon keep their health, and it gives no XP or EVs for the same reason.
  • In a City gym held by a player, the fight counts as against the player leader, not the City leader: it does not touch the City leader's unlock or penalty, and /pokegyms battles lists it as leader.
  • A rematch has to wait. See Rematch cooldown.
  • The penalty has its own switch. /pokegyms config vault turns it off: nobody pays or needs one to challenge.
  • It does not depend on the leader switch. /pokegyms config leader only stops new registrations; challenges keep working.

docs.title: Rematch cooldown
docs.text:
After you finish a challenge of a player leader, the same leader will not take you on again right away.

  • It starts when the challenge ends, won or lost. Forfeiting or running away counts as a loss. A battle the server stops, with no winner, starts no wait.
  • It is yours alone, and per gym. Another challenger can fight the same leader at once, and you can still fight other gyms' leaders.
  • Trying early is refused, and the message tells you the time left, such as "will take your challenge again in 45 min". The time is rounded up to whole minutes.
  • It lasts 60 minutes by default, and survives a server restart. A gym whose licence ends and is bought again starts with nobody waiting.
  • City leaders have no cooldown. It applies only to player leaders, not to the City (RCT) leaders.
  • Operators can change it with /pokegyms config rematch: cooldown_minutes sets the wait (0 means no wait), and enabled switches the whole cooldown off.

docs.title: Medals
docs.text:
Beating a player leader gives you a Gym Medal.

  • One medal, for every gym. It is a single generic item, with no art of its own per gym. It does not show in the creative tab; a medal only comes from a win.
  • It is signed. Hover it to read the gym ("Pewter City Gym" for a City gym, otherwise "Gym at" its coordinates), "Leader:" with the name of the player you beat, and "Won on" with the date of the win.
  • Only a win gives one. A loss, a forfeit, or a battle the server stops gives none, and so does a win against a City (RCT) leader: medals are for player leaders. The leader gets none either.
  • You get one per win. Winning the same gym again, after the rematch cooldown, gives another.
  • A full inventory is no loss. The medal drops at your feet.
  • With Badge It, the medal can be a badge. Badge It is optional. When it is installed, the holder's Team tab has a third row, Medal: hold one of its badges in your main hand and click it to register that badge as the gym's medal (you keep the badge). Winners then get a copy of that badge signed the same way, with the gym, the leader and the date in its lore. A badge crafted by hand carries no signature. Without Badge It, or before a badge is registered, winners get the generic medal. A gym's new licence starts without a badge.
  • Operators can switch it off with /pokegyms config medals enabled false: no win gives a medal, and medals already given stay.

docs.title: Level scaling
docs.text:
A gym leader's team fights at your level, whatever levels it was registered at. So does the team of every other Radical Cobblemon Trainers (RCT) trainer, including the ones wandering the world.

  • The level is your best Pokémon's. It is the highest level in your whole party, fainted Pokémon included, so a Pokémon you cannot send out still counts. The team scales up and down alike: a level 20 team meets a level 50 challenger at 50, and a level 80 team meets a level 30 one at 30.
  • Every Pokémon of the team is set to it, at full HP. It is capped at the server's maximum Pokémon level.
  • It covers every RCT trainer, in a gym or out of it. The City leaders and the trainers you meet in the world are RCT trainers, and so every battle against one is scaled. The player leaders are scaled too.
  • Each Pokémon takes the evolution stage of its new level. A registered Charizard faced at level 12 is a Charmander, and a Charmander faced at level 40 is a Charizard. It goes up and down alike, and only level evolutions are crossed, so a Vaporeon stays a Vaporeon. A Pokémon holding an Everstone keeps its species both ways. Where an evolution branches, the first one that applies is taken.
  • Empty move slots are filled for the new level. The moves a Pokémon was registered with stay in their slots, even one its new stage cannot learn. Each empty slot gets the newest level-up move its stage knows at the new level that it does not already have. A Pokémon registered with four moves fights with exactly those four.
  • Only the battle changes. The Team tab, a holder's registered team and RCT's trainer data keep their levels; the scaled Pokémon are copies made for that battle alone, so a trainer's team is the same when you meet it again at another level.
  • A format with its own fixed level keeps it. If the battle format sets a level for everyone, the opponent's team is not scaled.
  • Operators can switch it off with /pokegyms config scaling enabled false: teams then fight at their registered levels, RCT trainers' included. Battles already running keep the levels they started with. /pokegyms config evolution enabled false keeps only the evolution stages out: levels still scale, species stay as registered.

docs.title: The Gym Manager
docs.text:
Every gym has a Gym Manager: a lectern just inside the gym's door. It is put there as soon as the gym is found and the spot is loaded.

  • It cannot be broken in survival and drops nothing. A Gym Manager removed in creative comes back the next time its chunk loads.
  • It comes in three looks, wood, tech and Poké Ball. They behave the same; a City gym's is the Poké Ball one. All three are in the PokeGyms creative tab, for builders.
  • A Gym Manager placed by hand somewhere that is not a gym's spot belongs to no gym, and says so when right-clicked.

docs.title: The screen
docs.text:
Right-clicking a Gym Manager opens its screen, built on Cobblemon's summary screen:

  • The header names the gym by its city, such as Pewter City Gym, with a CITY tag, and who runs it: the City leader.
  • The Info tab, which everyone sees, gives the gym's kind (City gym), its status (Canonical) and its location (X, Z), with a short line about who runs it. At a City gym whose leader you beat, the line says you may buy its licence.
  • The Team tab, which only the holder sees, registers the gym's team.
  • The Vault tab, which only the holder sees, sets the gym's penalty and withdraws its vault.
  • The gym team panel on the side has six slots. They show the registered team by name and level, and stand empty while the gym has none.

The screen shows the gym as the server saw it when you opened it, and every button asks the server again before anything happens.

More tabs join the screen as features arrive. The Licence tab is already built; see Licences.

docs.title: Gym battles
docs.text:
A battle against an NPC trainer who stands inside a gym, such as a Cities & Structures gym leader, is a gym battle from its start until it ends. PokeGyms does not change the battle itself; it only marks it, so other mods can tell it apart. Mid-Battle EXP uses this to give more EXP in gyms.

Each gym battle knows its gym and who the challenger faces: the gym's leader, a disciple, or the City gym's canonical leader. Operators can list the gym battles running now with /pokegyms battles.

docs.title: For mod authors
docs.text:
Ask through com.shier.pokegyms.api.GymBattleApi. Every method is a JVM static, so a mod that does not depend on PokeGyms can call it by reflection:

Method Returns isGymBattle(battleId: UUID) Whether the Cobblemon battle is a gym battle. opponent(battleId: UUID) leader, disciple or canonical_leader; null when it is not a gym battle. marker(battleId: UUID) The whole marker (dimension, gym origin, opponent), for a mod compiled against PokeGyms; null when it is not a gym battle. 
val gym = runCatching {
    Class.forName("com.shier.pokegyms.api.GymBattleApi")
        .getMethod("isGymBattle", UUID::class.java)
        .invoke(null, battle.battleId) as Boolean
}.getOrDefault(false) // PokeGyms not installed

docs.title: Licences
docs.text:
A licence is what lets a player run a gym as its leader. The rules below are in the mod today.

A City gym's licence has to be earned

Every gym in this build is a City gym, led by an RCT leader. Its licence is for sale only to a player who beat that leader; to everyone else the Licence tab does not appear.

docs.title: The rules
docs.text:
• One licence per player on the whole server, whatever the dimension.
  • It costs 25,000 CobbleDollars by default, paid at the gym's Gym Manager. The server sets the price (Configuration).
  • A City gym sells its licence only to a player who beat its leader, at the same price and with the same one licence per player. Beating them is remembered even with licences switched off. While the gym is held its leader is gone; when the licence ends the leader is back and the gym is locked again for everyone, the former holder included.
  • It ends after 30 days without logging in by default, or when its holder renounces it. Either way a town gym goes vacant, anyone can buy it again, and the former holder may buy another (a City gym goes back to its leader, as above). The server checks when it starts and once a day after. With the days set to 0, a licence never expires.

docs.title: The Licence tab
docs.text:
At a vacant town gym, or a City gym whose leader you beat, the Gym Manager screen adds a Licence tab:

  • For a visitor: the price, how many CobbleDollars you have, and a Buy button. If you already hold a licence, the tab says which gym it is; if you are short, it says how much more you need. The server checks the price and your balance again when you click.
  • For the holder: when the licence expires, and a Renounce button, which asks for a second click to confirm.

docs.title: After a crash
docs.text:
When the server starts, it checks every licence against the gym it names, and the gym wins: a licence whose gym no longer names its player is dropped, a gym naming a holder the licence list forgot is added to it, and if one player ends up holding two gyms, the second goes vacant. Each fix is written to the server log. Licences of gyms in a dimension that is not loaded are left alone.

Switching licences off (Configuration) stops every gym from selling its licence. Licences already held stay, and still expire or can be renounced.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: If yours is not here, post it in the Discord: it files the ticket for you.

docs.title: There is no Gym Manager in a city
docs.text:
• The city has no gym building: Lavender and Pallet never have one, and the other cities do not always build theirs. /pokegyms gyms lists the gyms the server found in your dimension.
  • Cobblemon Cities & Structures is not installed on the server. Without it PokeGyms finds no gyms.
  • The spot has not loaded yet. The Gym Manager is placed when its chunk is loaded; walk into the gym.

docs.title: /pokegyms gyms says "No gyms recorded"
docs.text: No Cities & Structures city with a gym has loaded in that dimension yet, or Cities & Structures is missing. Gyms are found as their cities load, so explore first.

docs.title: The game will not start and names a mod
docs.text: One of the requirements is missing or older than PokeGyms needs. The message says which and which version; install that one.

docs.title: Right-clicking a Gym Manager says it belongs to no gym
docs.text: That lectern was placed by hand, not by PokeGyms. Only the Gym Manager standing at a gym's own spot opens the gym's screen.

docs.title: There is no Licence tab
docs.text: That is expected in this build: no gym sells a licence yet (Licences).

docs.title: The config file did not take my change
docs.text: It is read when the server starts. On a live server, use /pokegyms config instead (Commands & Configuration). If the file is not valid JSON, the server runs on the defaults and says so in its log.

docs.title: The Gym Vault
docs.text:
A player-held gym has a vault: the CobbleDollars that challengers lost to its leader. The holder sets the penalty a challenger risks, and takes the vault's money when they like.

Everything here is on the Vault tab of the Gym Manager, which only the gym's holder sees. City gyms led by an RCT leader have no vault; their penalty is destroyed.

docs.title: Setting the penalty
docs.text:
The tab shows the Penalty and what the Vault holds.

  • Click the Penalty row to raise it by a tenth of the server's range. Shift-click lowers it. Past either end it wraps round to the other.
  • It stays within the server's range, vault.penalty_min to vault.penalty_max (100 to 10,000 CobbleDollars by default; see Configuration). The server checks it again, so no other amount gets through.
  • A new holder starts on the least.
  • It is locked while your leader is battling. You are told to change it when the battle ends, so a challenger never pays more than they agreed to.

docs.title: Challengers
docs.text:
• You need the penalty in hand to challenge the leader. There are no debts: if you carry less, you are told what it costs and what you have, and the fight does not start.
  • Losing pays it. A loss, a forfeit or running away moves exactly the penalty from you into the vault. You are told what you paid.
  • Winning costs nothing, and neither does a battle the server stops with no winner.
  • If the gym's licence ends during the battle, or you spent the money meanwhile, nothing moves.

docs.title: Withdrawing
docs.text: Withdraw appears when the vault holds money and moves all of it to your CobbleDollars. If CobbleDollars refuses the payment, the vault keeps its money and you can try again.

docs.title: When the licence ends
docs.text: Renouncing, expiring or a takeover pays the whole vault to the holder before the gym goes vacant. A holder who is offline gets it on their next login, and is told then. The money is not lost if CobbleDollars refuses it: it is kept for the next login.

docs.title: Switching it off
docs.text: With vault.enabled off, no player leader charges a penalty and a challenger needs none to start. The tab says penalties are off; vaults keep what they hold, can still be withdrawn, and are still paid out when a licence ends.
